bank.q: You approach a red octagonal sign. What must you do?
a: Come to a complete stop, then proceed when it is safe
Slow down and continue if the way looks clear
Stop only if another vehicle is approaching
bank.why: A stop sign requires a full stop every time, whether or not anyone else is there.

bank.q: What does a downward-pointing triangle with a red border mean?
a: Give way to traffic on the road you are joining
bank.why: An inverted triangle is Yield / Give Way: slow down, and stop if needed, to let others pass first.

bank.q: A solid white circle with a horizontal white bar on red means:
bank.why: A red disc with a white bar is No Entry. Entering against it means driving into oncoming traffic.

bank.q: You are driving and an emergency vehicle approaches with lights and siren. You should:
a: Pull over to the side where safe and stop until it passes
Speed up to stay ahead of it
Brake hard immediately wherever you are
bank.why: Move out of its path safely and stop. Stopping abruptly in a live lane can cause a collision.

bank.q: What is the main purpose of a vehicle's headrest?
a: To reduce neck injury in a rear-end collision
To make long journeys more comfortable
To hold the seatbelt in place
bank.why: Head restraints limit how far the head snaps back in an impact, reducing whiplash.

bank.q: In wet conditions, your stopping distance compared with dry roads is:
bank.why: Wet roads roughly double stopping distance, so following gaps must grow to match.

bank.q: What does a flashing amber or yellow traffic light mean?
a: Stop as if at a stop sign
The light is broken; ignore it
bank.why: Flashing amber means slow down and proceed carefully. A flashing red is the one that means stop.

bank.q: Before changing lanes you should:
a: Check mirrors, signal, then check the blind spot before moving
bank.why: Mirror, signal, blind spot, then move. Mirrors alone leave a vehicle-sized gap unchecked.

bank.q: When are you permitted to use a mobile phone in your hand while driving?
a: Never while the vehicle is in motion
bank.why: Handheld phone use while driving is prohibited in the overwhelming majority of countries.

bank.q: Approaching a roundabout, you generally give way to:
bank.why: Traffic already circulating has priority. Which side that traffic comes from depends on the country.

driver.note: Road rules are the most general knowledge here, so the test is the longest.

bank.q: What is the most protective item of motorcycle clothing?
bank.why: Head injury is the leading cause of motorcycle deaths. A fitted, certified helmet matters most.

bank.q: 'Counter-steering' at speed means:
a: Pressing the bar on the side you want to turn toward
Turning the bars away from the corner and leaning back
bank.why: Above walking pace you push the bar on the side you want to go, which leans the bike into the turn.

bank.q: Most of a motorcycle's braking power comes from:
bank.why: Weight shifts forward under braking, so the front wheel does the majority of the work.

bank.q: Why should a rider avoid the centre of an older lane?
a: Oil and fluid build up there and reduce grip
It is illegal to ride there
It is the fastest-wearing part of the tyre
bank.why: Dropped oil collects along the centre strip, which becomes slick especially in first rain.

bank.q: In a car driver's blind spot, the safest action is to:
a: Change position so you are visible or move clearly past
Sit still and hold your lane
bank.why: Do not linger where you cannot be seen. Alter your position or pass through decisively.

bank.q: Riding in heavy rain, you should:
a: Increase following distance and brake more gently
Ride in the centre of the lane
Follow closely to stay out of spray
bank.why: Grip is reduced, so lengthen your gap and use smoother inputs.

bank.q: A motorcycle's tyres are most vulnerable when:
a: Cold, at the very start of a ride
At the end of a long motorway run
Fully warmed on a dry day
bank.why: Cold tyres offer noticeably less grip. The first few kilometres deserve restraint.

motorcycle.note: Assumes you already hold or understand basic road rules.

bank.q: A vessel showing a red light on its left side and a green light on its right is:
a: Being viewed from ahead or from its port side
bank.why: Port is red, starboard is green. Seeing both means you are looking at its bow.

bank.q: Who is responsible for the wake a boat creates?
a: The operator of the boat that made it
bank.why: Operators are responsible for damage or injury caused by their own wake.

bank.q: The single most important piece of safety equipment on a small boat is:
a: A properly fitted life jacket for every person aboard
bank.why: Most drowning victims in small-boat incidents were not wearing a life jacket.

bank.q: Before departing, a float plan should be left with someone ashore because:
a: It tells rescuers where to look and when to worry
It logs fuel use for tax
bank.why: If you do not return, a float plan turns an open-ended search into a targeted one.

bank.q: Two power-driven vessels approaching head-on should:
a: Each alter course to starboard and pass port to port
Hold course and sound one blast
bank.why: Head-on, both turn to starboard and pass left side to left side.

bank.q: Carbon monoxide aboard a boat is most dangerous:
a: Near the stern and swim platform while the engine runs
Only in enclosed cabins at night
At anchor with the engine off
bank.why: Exhaust can pool around the stern. Swimmers and passengers there have been poisoned.

boating.note: Navigation lights, right of way and what to do before you leave the dock.

bank.q: The first rule of firearm safety is:
a: Treat every firearm as if it is loaded
bank.why: Every other rule follows from assuming it is loaded, every time, without exception.

bank.q: Where should the muzzle point at all times?
a: In a safe direction, never at anything you are unwilling to destroy
bank.why: Muzzle discipline is what makes an accidental discharge survivable.

bank.q: Your finger belongs:
a: Off the trigger and along the frame until you intend to fire
On the trigger whenever the firearm is held
Inside the guard when aiming only
bank.why: Most negligent discharges come from a finger inside the trigger guard too early.

bank.q: Before firing you must:
a: Identify your target and what lies beyond it
bank.why: Bullets travel past and through targets. You are responsible for where they stop.

bank.q: Firearms and ammunition should generally be stored:
a: Separately, secured, and inaccessible to children
Loaded and together for quick access
bank.why: Secure, separate storage is the standard almost everywhere, and is what keeps households safe.

bank.q: If a round fails to fire, you should:
a: Keep it pointed safely downrange and wait before handling
Strike the primer again at once
bank.why: A hangfire can go off seconds later. Keep it pointed safely and wait before opening the action.

firearms.note: Safety rules only. Every question here has one defensible answer.

bank.q: The main purpose of hunting seasons and bag limits is:
bank.why: Regulated seasons and limits are a conservation tool, designed to keep populations viable.

bank.q: Wearing blaze orange or fluorescent clothing is required in many places because:
a: Most game animals cannot see it, but other hunters can
bank.why: Deer are dichromats and do not register blaze orange the way humans do, so it protects without spooking game.

bank.q: The safest way to cross a fence with a firearm alone is:
a: Unload it, place it through the fence, then cross
Keep it loaded but on safe
bank.why: Unload first. Crossing obstacles while carrying a loaded firearm is a classic cause of injury.

bank.q: An ethical shot is one that:
a: Is within your range and likely to be quick and clean
Is at the largest animal visible
bank.why: Hunting ethics centre on a quick, certain kill and not wounding an animal you cannot recover.

bank.q: Before hunting on land you do not own, you must:
a: Nothing, if the land is unfenced
bank.why: Hunting without permission is trespass nearly everywhere, fenced or not.

bank.q: Identifying your target before shooting matters most because:
a: Movement or colour alone has caused hunters to shoot people
bank.why: Shooting at sound or movement is how hunters kill other hunters. Positive identification is absolute.

bank.q: Catch limits and size limits exist mainly to:
a: Let fish breed before they are taken, keeping stocks alive
bank.why: Size limits usually allow fish to spawn at least once before they can be legally kept.

bank.q: If you intend to release a fish, you should:
a: Keep it wet, handle it minimally and support its body
Keep it out of water to recover
Squeeze it to remove the hook
bank.why: Gills are delicate and easily fatal to damage. Wet hands, minimal air time, support the body.

bank.q: Invasive species spread between waters mainly by:
a: Unwashed boats, gear and live bait moved between lakes
bank.why: Cleaning and drying gear between waters is the main defence against transferring invasives.

bank.q: Monofilament line left on a bank is dangerous because:
a: It entangles birds and wildlife and lasts for decades
bank.why: Discarded line persists for a very long time and routinely entangles wildlife.

fishing.note: Short test. The knowledge is narrow and mostly about not wrecking the water.

bank.q: The four forces acting on an aircraft in flight are:
bank.why: Lift opposes weight; thrust opposes drag. Steady flight is those pairs in balance.

bank.q: An aircraft stalls when:
a: The wing exceeds its critical angle of attack
Airspeed falls below a fixed number in all conditions
bank.why: A stall is about angle of attack, not speed. A wing can stall at any airspeed and any attitude.

bank.q: Before every flight a pilot must:
a: Complete a preflight inspection of the aircraft
File a flight plan in all cases
Run the engine for ten minutes
bank.why: The preflight walkaround is a non-negotiable check of airframe, controls, fuel and oil.

bank.q: 'See and avoid' means:
a: Pilots are responsible for visually watching for other traffic
bank.why: In visual conditions the responsibility to spot and avoid traffic rests with the pilot.

bank.q: Flying into deteriorating weather without an instrument rating is dangerous because:
a: Losing visual reference can cause spatial disorientation within minutes
bank.why: Continued VFR into instrument conditions is one of the most consistently fatal decisions in aviation.

pilot.note: Specialist knowledge, so fewer questions - but you must get them all.

bank.q: The most important rule in scuba diving is:
a: Never hold your breath while ascending
Always ascend faster than your bubbles
bank.why: Air in the lungs expands on ascent. Holding your breath can rupture lung tissue.

bank.q: Decompression sickness is caused by:
a: Dissolved nitrogen forming bubbles when you ascend too fast
bank.why: Nitrogen absorbed under pressure must be released slowly, which is why ascent rate is controlled.

bank.q: A safety stop is normally made at:
a: The deepest point of the dive
bank.why: A three-minute stop around five metres gives dissolved gas extra time to come out safely.

bank.q: You should always dive:
a: With a buddy and an agreed plan
bank.why: The buddy system exists because underwater problems escalate quickly without a second person.

bank.q: Flying too soon after diving is dangerous because:
a: Cabin pressure is lower, which can trigger decompression sickness
bank.why: Ascending to altitude repeats the pressure drop. Surface intervals before flying are essential.

scuba.note: Specialist knowledge, so fewer questions - but you must get them all.
